title: Generative embedding distinguishes recorded two-year depression trajectories
summary: In a retrospective reanalysis of 85 NESDA patients, a support-vector classifier using modeled brain connectivity distinguished chronic depression from rapid remission with 79% balanced accuracy in nested cross-validation. The February 2020 journal analysis follows a September 2019 preprint. Small groups, reused data and uncontrolled treatment limit clinical interpretation.
ai_technology: Linear support vector machine with dynamic-causal-model generative embedding
organization: University of Zurich; ETH Zurich; Radboud University; King’s College London; University of Melbourne; Amsterdam UMC; Leiden University; University of Groningen

evidence.tested: Baseline face-processing fMRI and available two-year follow-up identified 39 rapid-remission, 31 gradual-improvement and 15 chronic-course patients. SVM hyperparameters were optimized using training-only inner five-fold cross-validation inside leave-one-person-out evaluation. Chronic versus rapid-remission classification reached 79% balanced accuracy and ROC AUC .87; gradual versus rapid remission reached 61% but did not survive the stated multiple-comparison correction, and chronic versus gradual improvement was at chance.
evidence.unknown: This is retrospective prognostic modeling in a selected 85-person cohort, not prospective evaluation of a frozen model. The chronic group comprised only 15 patients; age differed and source-reported age adjustment reduced balanced accuracy to 74%. Treatments and intervening life events were not standardized. An earlier Schmaal analysis used the same source cohort and clinical-trajectory grouping, so this reanalysis is not independent confirmation or first discovery of those trajectories. Source footnotes warn that McNemar comparisons between cross-validated classifiers may be optimistic. The original preprint API dates version1 to September 18, 2019; only its metadata/abstract were available in this review, so journal-specific metrics are not backdated. No individualized-treatment benefit or causal neural mechanism is established.
evidence.ai_role: A learned SVM classified later clinical-trajectory labels using posterior connectivity parameters from a conventional generative model; the AI contribution is the discriminative classifier, not an assumption that causal-model terminology proves causation.

source_review.scope: Original primary computational training, clinical/sample definition, represented Results and bounded Discussion/limitations actually read; earlier primary preprint API metadata/abstract read, not its full tables.
